small_guidance:
- The atomic_add accumulator over (N, OW) is fine but the inner BLOCK_OH loop serializes oh rows; try smaller BLOCK_OH (4 or 8) with more programs in the OH grid dimension to expose parallelism, and add configs with BLOCK_W=256 to better amortize the weight loads. Also include num_stages=3 variants since the dot is the hot path.
- The weight tile (BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_IC=64) is reloaded for every (kh, kw) and every oh inside the program. Hoist the kh/kw weight loads outside the oh_local loop by reordering loops to (kh, kw, oh_local) so each weight tile is loaded once per program, and reuse across BLOCK_OH rows.
- Replace the `acc` fp32 scratch + separate gelu_bias_kernel with a fused epilogue: have one program own a full (n, ow) column (persistent over OH), so the partial sum lives in registers and GELU+bias is applied before the single store — eliminates the atomic_add traffic entirely.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as one program per (n, ow_tile) that is persistent along OH: iterate oh inside the kernel, compute the min over OC per (oh, ow) on the fly, accumulate the sum into a register vector of length BLOCK_W, then apply GELU+bias and store once. This removes the atomic_add, removes the second kernel launch, and keeps the BLOCK_OC×BLOCK_IC weight tiles resident across many oh values.
- Reorder the accumulation as (kh, kw) outer, (oh, ow) inner so each weight slice w[:, :, kh, kw] is loaded once and reused across all valid oh in the column; the stride-2/pad-1 index math means only ⌈OH/SH⌉≈64 input rows contribute per output column, so per-(kh,kw) you do a tight loop of ~64 dots into a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_W) tile, then min-reduce along OC and sum into the column accumulator.
- Consider channels_last input layout (N, IH, IW, IC) so the GEMM-K (IC) load is contiguous; combined with packing weight as (KH, KW, IC, OC) this turns the inner tl.dot into a clean contiguous matmul and should remove the remaining bandwidth bottleneck on the 4090.
